Now I see the issue! The `_MarkupEscapeHelper` class has a `__getitem__` method that returns `self.__class__(self.obj[key], self.escape)`. This is supposed to wrap dictionary lookups. But the issue is that when you do `Markup(template) % dict`, the `__mod__` method wraps the entire dict object in `_MarkupEscapeHelper`, but then Python's string formatting tries to iterate over it and call `__getitem__` on it.

turns.content:
Interesting! So Python's default behavior is to raise an `AttributeError` when you try to use dot notation on a dict, but MarkupSafe is raising a `KeyError`. This is actually a bug in the `_MarkupEscapeHelper.__getitem__` method!

The problem is that when Python's string formatting encounters `%(user.name)s`, it tries to access the dictionary with the key `'user.name'` (a single string key), not as nested access. But the `_MarkupEscapeHelper` is wrapping the dict and when it tries to do `self.obj[key]`, it's doing the same thing.
